summary: Titanium disulfide thin films were grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using TiCl4 and H2S as precursors at temperatures between 400–500 °C. The films were deposited on various substrates including soda-lime glass, silicon, and noble metals. The growth rate varied depending on the substrate, with hexagonal (001)-oriented growth observed on ZnS and platinum. The study aimed to explore the ALD process for TiS2 and its potential applications in nanostructures and batteries.
